name: cues
title: Gamestage cues
description: The game-feel runtime: juice level from none to maximum, sound and haptic playback behind an adapter, and the host's own mute honoured alongside a best-effort OS silent-switch signal. It plays nothing itself; the token file says what a cue means and this hands the allowed ones to the host. No asset files yet (GSUI-38 attaches them), so today playing a cue means recording that it fired, in order.

files.content:
/**
 * The cue vocabulary: names and intent, mirroring the `sfx` and `haptic`
 * groups in packages/tokens/tokens.json (BDS-003). Intent, never a file path;
 * GSUI-38 attaches real assets to these same names later.
 *
 * Each entry also carries a tier, which is how a juice level gates it (see
 * juice.ts). An `essential` cue is the confirmation of what the player just
 * did, or a settled outcome, and juice never silences it: only mute does.
 * `standard` and `celebration` are the flourish on top, and a lower juice
 * level trims celebration first, then standard.
 */

export type CueKind = 'sfx' | 'haptic'

export type CueTier = 'essential' | 'standard' | 'celebration'

export type SfxName =
  | 'press'
  | 'select'
  | 'commit'
  | 'correct'
  | 'wrong'
  | 'score'
  | 'streak'
  | 'xp'
  | 'rankUp'
  | 'hint'
  | 'countdown'
  | 'go'
  | 'tick'
  | 'reveal'
  | 'reward'
  | 'collect'
  | 'levelUp'
  | 'win'
  | 'celebrate'

export type HapticName = 'light' | 'medium' | 'heavy' | 'success' | 'error'

export type CueName = SfxName | HapticName

export interface CueEntry {
  tier: CueTier
  /** The intent, copied from tokens.json. Never a file path. */
  intent: string
}

export const SFX_CATALOGUE: Record<SfxName, CueEntry> = {
  press: { tier: 'essential', intent: 'tick' },
  select: { tier: 'essential', intent: 'soft click' },
  commit: { tier: 'essential', intent: 'lock, weighted' },
  correct: { tier: 'essential', intent: 'bright, short' },
  wrong: { tier: 'essential', intent: 'low, dull, never harsh' },
  score: { tier: 'essential', intent: 'tick per 10 pts during count-up' },
  tick: { tier: 'essential', intent: 'per second when timer critical' },
  streak: { tier: 'standard', intent: 'pitched by n' },
  xp: { tier: 'standard', intent: 'rising with amount' },
  rankUp: { tier: 'standard', intent: 'whoosh up; rank lost is silent' },
  hint: { tier: 'standard', intent: 'single chime' },
  countdown: { tier: 'standard', intent: '3 pips' },
  go: { tier: 'standard', intent: 'accent hit' },
  reveal: { tier: 'celebration', intent: 'build then sfx.reward' },
  reward: { tier: 'celebration', intent: 'shimmer' },
  collect: { tier: 'celebration', intent: 'pop into inventory' },
  levelUp: { tier: 'celebration', intent: 'rising 3-note' },
  win: { tier: 'celebration', intent: 'fanfare 1.5s or less' },
  celebrate: { tier: 'celebration', intent: 'burst 1.5s or less' },
}

export const HAPTIC_CATALOGUE: Record<HapticName, CueEntry> = {
  light: { tier: 'essential', intent: 'tap, select, collect' },
  error: { tier: 'essential', intent: 'wrong, life lost' },
  medium: { tier: 'standard', intent: 'commit, streak, GO' },
  success: { tier: 'standard', intent: 'correct, reward, level up' },
  heavy: { tier: 'celebration', intent: 'win' },
}

/** Looks a cue up by kind and name. Undefined for a name outside the vocabulary. */
export function describeCue(kind: CueKind, name: string): CueEntry | undefined {
  const table: Record<string, CueEntry> = kind === 'sfx' ? SFX_CATALOGUE : HAPTIC_CATALOGUE
  return table[name]
}

export { GameFeelProvider, useGameFeel } from './feel'
export type { GameFeelProviderProps, GameFeelValue, GameFeelCueEvent } from './feel'

export type { JuiceLevel } from './juice'
export { allowsCue } from './juice'

export type { CueKind, CueName, SfxName, HapticName, CueTier, CueEntry } from './cue-catalogue'
export { describeCue, SFX_CATALOGUE, HAPTIC_CATALOGUE } from './cue-catalogue'

export type { SoundAdapter } from './sound-adapter'
export { createHtmlAudioAdapter, createWebAudioAdapter } from './sound-adapter'

export { canVibrate, fireHaptic } from './haptics'

docs: Wrap the part of the tree that plays a game in <GameFeelProvider>, then call useGameFeel().cue(name, kind) wherever a state change happens: a settled correct fires cue('correct', 'sfx'), a light tap fires cue('light', 'haptic'). Pass `muted` from the host's own mute switch; the provider ORs it with a best-effort OS silent-switch signal, so either can silence sound and neither can force it back on. Pass `juice` ('none' | 'reduced' | 'standard' | 'maximum') to scale celebration: essential cues, the confirmation of what the player just did, are never gated by juice, only by mute. `hapticsOff` gates navigator.vibrate independently of sound. No sound or haptic actually plays yet: GSUI-38 attaches real assets to the same cue names.
